responses.reason: R1 correctly notes that Candidate A's simulated delivery failure fails the entire batch (handleInvite branches once on state.delivery === 'failure') and retries the whole list, with no per-address partial-success state. My 4 credited breadth - validation, loading, failure, retry, seat limit, paused/resume - but 'excellent' completeness should include partial failure when several addresses are invited in one action, which Candidate B does implement. That is a real gap, so I revise to 3.
responses.evidence: Round-1 input condition-a/implementation/app.js handleInvite (single delivery === 'failure' branch) and index.html prototype select 'Invitation delivery: Succeeds/Fails'; R1 product-onboarding-r2.json candidate_a interaction_completeness rationale

responses.reason: Axe is clean and every control is named, which R1's 4 rests on. But axe cannot detect demo chrome covering content: at 390px the floating prototype panel sits over the Description field's hint and 'Optional' tag (my mobile-overlap.png). An obscured form label is viewport behaviour and is part of this dimension, so an automated-clean result does not cancel it. R1 acknowledges the overlap but files it only under visual hierarchy; I keep 3.

Candidate B's analysis explains why project precedes invitations and explicitly treats the invite step as a gate risk with mitigations (analysis.md lines 55 and 106), and it states costs for role-card height and the one-role-per-screen choice. R1's objection is the unexamined welcome screen and the 3-row invite cap; the welcome cost is a flow problem already priced into ux_reasoning (3), and the 3-row cap is a prototype control rather than evidence that the trade-off reasoning is weak. I keep 4 instead of double-counting the same choice.
responses.evidence: R1 product-onboarding-r2.json candidate_b design_judgment; round-1 analysis.md sections 2 and 6; my evidence/product-onboarding-r2/b/desktop-welcome.png

differences_remaining: candidate_a.accessibility_responsiveness: R2 keeps 3 (mobile demo panel obscures the Description hint/label) vs R1 4 (clean axe and named controls).
candidate_b.design_judgment: R2 keeps 4 (welcome cost already counted in ux; documented trade-offs) vs R1 3 (unexamined welcome and 3-row cap).
candidate_a.interaction_completeness was revised from 4 to 3 and is no longer contested.
summary: Three dimensions were disputed. I revised Candidate A's interaction completeness to 3 because its invite failure is all-or-nothing with whole-list retry, which R1 correctly identified as a completeness gap; I maintained the A accessibility score because the mobile overlay covers a form hint even though axe is clean, and maintained B's design judgment because the welcome-screen cost is already reflected in the UX score rather than being a separate reasoning failure.
